title: What Is Uttarakhand's New Chakbandi Land Policy?
desc: Uttarakhand's 2026 voluntary land consolidation policy lets hill farmers in 275 villages combine scattered plots into one block.
why: The state cabinet approved a Voluntary Land Consolidation Incentive Policy in 2026 to merge scattered hill farmland, and villages are being taken up under it this year.
keyPoints: The Uttarakhand cabinet approved a Voluntary Land Consolidation Incentive Policy in May 2026 for hill district farmers.
It covers 275 villages across the state's 11 hill districts, with five villages taken up per district each year.
Consolidation needs every landowner's consent, and only villages with no pending land dispute are selected.
Farmers get an incentive once their village's scattered plots are successfully combined into single blocks.

sections.h: What is Uttarakhand's chakbandi (land consolidation) policy?
p: Uttarakhand's Voluntary Land Consolidation Incentive Policy, approved by the state cabinet in May 2026, lets farmers in hill districts combine their scattered plots into one block with everyone's consent. It covers 275 villages across the state's 11 hill districts, with five villages taken up in each district every year under the Revenue Department.

Only villages with no pending land dispute are picked for the scheme. The goal is to make small, broken-up hill farms easier to irrigate and cultivate, and to reduce migration from hill villages by making farming there more viable.

sections.h: How does chakbandi actually work for a landowner?
p: A landowner does not lose land under this scheme, their scattered plots are re-arranged into one combined holding of similar value, in the same village. The process is consent-based: every affected landowner in the selected village has to agree before the Revenue Department carries out the consolidation.

Once the swap is completed and recorded, the farmer's khatauni (land record) is updated to show the new, consolidated plot. Incentives under the policy are released after a village's consolidation is successfully completed, not before.

sections.h: Can a landowner be forced to join, or refuse?
p: No. The policy is voluntary, so a landowner cannot be forced to swap plots against their wishes. If even a few landowners in a selected village do not agree, the department works through the consultation again before any consolidation goes ahead there.

A village is also kept out of the scheme entirely if it has an unresolved boundary, inheritance or title dispute, since such disputes have to be sorted out first through the normal revenue or civil court process.

whatToDo: Ask the village patwari or the tehsil revenue office whether your village has been selected for consolidation this year.
Keep your khatauni and khasra land records updated and in your own name before any consolidation talks begin.
Settle any pending boundary or inheritance dispute first, since disputed villages are not taken up under the scheme.
Get the final combined plot details and boundaries confirmed in writing before agreeing to any plot swap.

hi.title: उत्तराखंड की नई चकबंदी नीति क्या है?
keyPoints: मई 2026 में उत्तराखंड कैबिनेट ने पहाड़ी किसानों के लिए स्वैच्छिक भूमि चकबंदी प्रोत्साहन नीति मंजूर की।
यह नीति राज्य के 11 पहाड़ी जिलों के 275 गांवों में लागू होगी, हर जिले में हर साल पांच गांव लिए जाएंगे।
चकबंदी के लिए सभी भूस्वामियों की सहमति जरूरी है, और जिन गांवों में जमीन विवाद लंबित है उन्हें नहीं चुना जाता।
गांव में चकबंदी पूरी होने के बाद ही किसानों को प्रोत्साहन राशि दी जाती है।
